root_cause: scripts/wp08_release_github.py implements ReleaseRun discovery by listing all open repository issues through only ten 100-row pages. GitHub caps this unfiltered query before historical issue #696, while release_issues() treats the truncated result as complete and find_release_issue() interprets absence as no active authority. The issue-comment controller therefore returns successfully without acting, and authorize() can also miss the same live ledger.
causal_chain: The repository has more than 1000 newer open issue/PR rows than ReleaseRun ledger #696.
GitHubAPI.list_issues() requests only pages 1 through 10 and does not constrain the query to WP-08 ReleaseRun ledgers.
Page 10 ends at issue #958 and GitHub rejects page 11, so #696 is absent from the returned collection.
release_issues() and find_release_issue() accept the bounded generic collection as complete.
handle_issue_comment() finds no active ledger and returns without executing the exact authorized retirement command.
The same false absence can bypass authorize()'s single-active-run guard.
rejected_hypotheses: The retirement command text or run ID was malformed; rejected because the posted comment exactly matches the repository regex and current run ID.
The commenter lacked authority; rejected because the authenticated actor was repository owner toctionyan.
The underlying WP-08 run was nonterminal or successful; rejected because run 31716787445 is completed with conclusion failure.
Manually edit and close issue #696; rejected because the issue explicitly forbids hand editing and the coordinator owns ReleaseRun transitions.
Start a second ReleaseRun while #696 remains open; rejected because it violates the single-active-run hard invariant.
